strings.name: David R. Liu
strings.summary: David Liu combines chemistry, protein evolution and genome engineering. His teams developed base editing, prime editing and continuous directed-evolution tools. Working at Harvard, Broad and HHMI, he advances precise DNA modification and genetic-disease treatment research, with students, clinical teams and collaborators.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Advances research on base editing, prime editing and related technologies, expanding tools for precise gene modification and their potential biomedical applications.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Harvard bachelor's degree; PhD, University of California, Berkeley
strings.highlights.h1.title: Expanding precise editing
strings.highlights.h1.text: His teams' base and prime editors broaden options for targeted DNA substitutions, insertions and deletions.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Connecting research and applications
strings.highlights.h2.text: Related tools entered multiple clinical trials; he received the 2025 Breakthrough Prize in Life Sciences and the 2026 Bower science award.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Bower science award
strings.timeline.t1.text: The Franklin Institute honored his precise gene-editing technologies and contributions to scientific and medical applications.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Breakthrough Prize in Life Sciences
strings.timeline.t2.text: Recognized for base and prime editing, he emphasized students' and collaborators' contributions.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Developing prime editing
strings.timeline.t3.text: His team published a genome-editing method for targeted substitutions, insertions and deletions.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Developing base editing
strings.timeline.t4.text: His team introduced conversion of particular DNA base pairs without creating double-strand breaks.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Publishing PACE
strings.timeline.t5.text: With Kevin Esvelt and Jacob Carlson, he published phage-assisted continuous-evolution research.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becoming an HHMI investigator
strings.timeline.t6.text: He gained Howard Hughes Medical Institute support and became a full professor at Harvard that year.
strings.timeline.t7.title: PhD and Harvard appointment
strings.timeline.t7.text: After his Berkeley doctorate, he became an assistant professor of chemistry and chemical biology at Harvard.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Harvard undergraduate degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: He graduated from Harvard College before pursuing doctoral research at Berkeley.
